blocks.directed: Here sat means being, reality, what is.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: We already studied this in the previous chapter.
blocks.directed: We already studied this in the previous chapter.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: It is connected with √as, to be.
blocks.directed: It is connected with √as, to be.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta draws out the deeper significance of immediate transformation as entry into the reality of being.
blocks.directed: Abhinavagupta draws out the deeper significance of immediate transformation as entry into the reality of being.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The transformation is not a progression toward a distant object.
blocks.directed: The transformation is not a progression toward a distant object.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: It is an unveiling of the ground that makes every present experience possible.
blocks.directed: It is an unveiling of the ground that makes every present experience possible.

blocks.text: Tanmukhatām eti

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: He then explains the root text's phrase about the mantramudrāgaṇa becoming oriented toward the practitioner.
blocks.directed: He then explains the root text's phrase about the mantramudrāgaṇa becoming oriented toward the practitioner.

blocks.text: तन्मुखतामेति

blocks.text: “It comes to face that,” or “becomes oriented toward that.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “It comes to face that,” or “becomes oriented toward that.”

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The abstract -tā gives the condition of being oriented toward something.
blocks.directed: The abstract -tā gives the condition of being oriented toward something.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw

blocks.directed: And eti, from √i, means “goes,” “comes,” or “enters into a condition.”

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The passage explains that the powers become oriented toward their supreme nature.
blocks.directed: The passage explains that the powers become oriented toward their supreme nature.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Contrast this with the unawakened subject, in whom that nature is concealed.
blocks.directed: Contrast this with the unawakened subject, in whom that nature is concealed.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Again, the issue is not necessarily that objectively separate beings literally turn around in physical space.
blocks.directed: Again, the issue is not necessarily that objectively separate beings literally turn around in physical space.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The commentary is interpreting the orientation of the powers of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The commentary is interpreting the orientation of the powers of consciousness.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The ordinary person and the awakened person
blocks.directed: The ordinary person and the awakened person

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The limited subject becomes absorbed in the object.
blocks.directed: The limited subject becomes absorbed in the object.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The awakened subject recognises the conscious ground of the object and the act of apprehension.
blocks.directed: The awakened subject recognises the conscious ground of the object and the act of apprehension.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Both can perceive exactly the same external scene.
blocks.directed: Both can perceive exactly the same external scene.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Both can speak.
blocks.directed: Both can speak.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Both can remember.
blocks.directed: Both can remember.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Both can act.
blocks.directed: Both can act.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: But the meaning of the experience differs.
blocks.directed: But the meaning of the experience differs.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Take the simple act of seeing a tree.
blocks.directed: Take the simple act of seeing a tree.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Ordinarily:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Ordinarily:

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: “I am here. The tree is there. I am a little consciousness inside this body looking at an external object.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am here. The tree is there. I am a little consciousness inside this body looking at an external object.”

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: In the Pratyabhijñā analysis, the tree's appearance and the limited subject's apprehension both arise within consciousness.
blocks.directed: In the Pratyabhijñā analysis, the tree's appearance and the limited subject's apprehension both arise within consciousness.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: Recognition does not require denying the tree's differentiated appearance.
blocks.directed: Recognition does not require denying the tree's differentiated appearance.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: It requires understanding the relation between the tree, its manifestness, and the ultimate subject.
blocks.directed: It requires understanding the relation between the tree, its manifestness, and the ultimate subject.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The empirical distinction between observer and tree continues to function.
blocks.directed: The empirical distinction between observer and tree continues to function.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: The metaphysical assumption of absolute separation is no longer taken as ultimate.
blocks.directed: The metaphysical assumption of absolute separation is no longer taken as ultimate.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: That is the kind of change Abhinavagupta is explaining.
blocks.directed: That is the kind of change Abhinavagupta is explaining.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: But then he reaches the word muhūrta.
blocks.directed: But then he reaches the word muhūrta.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: A short period of time.
blocks.directed: A short period of time.

blocks.section: IX. The Word *Sadyaḥ* Contains a Clue to *Sat*: Immediate Aw
blocks.text: And the discussion takes a distinctly unsettling turn.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness Isn't in Time?
blocks.directed: [long pause] Ten. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness Isn't in Time?

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Kashmir Series pp. 245-246 - Gnoli p. 270
blocks.directed: Kashmir Series pp. 245-246 - Gnoli p. 270

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta writes:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Abhinavagupta writes:

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: अत एव मुहूर्तम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] अत एव मुहूर्तम्

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: ata eva muhūrtam.
blocks.directed: ata eva muhūrtam.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: “Therefore, a moment.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Therefore, a moment.”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But what does muhūrta mean?
blocks.directed: But what does muhūrta mean?

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Ordinarily it refers to a division of time, conventionally one-thirtieth of a day and night, or forty-eight minutes in the standard reckoning.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily it refers to a division of time, conventionally one-thirtieth of a day and night, or forty-eight minutes in the standard reckoning.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: And yet Abhinavagupta immediately qualifies it:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And yet Abhinavagupta immediately qualifies it:

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: अकालकलितत्वेऽपि परकलनापेक्षया उन्मेषमात्रम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] अकालकलितत्वेऽपि परकलनापेक्षया उन्मेषमात्रम्

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: akālakalitatve 'pi parakalanāpekṣayā unmeṣamātram.
blocks.directed: akālakalitatve 'pi parakalanāpekṣayā unmeṣamātram.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: “Although it is not delimited by time, relative to another mode of reckoning it is merely an opening or flash.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Although it is not delimited by time, relative to another mode of reckoning it is merely an opening or flash.”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Now the metaphysical problem becomes serious.
blocks.directed: Now the metaphysical problem becomes serious.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: If consciousness is the ground of time, it cannot itself be an ordinary object contained within time.
blocks.directed: If consciousness is the ground of time, it cannot itself be an ordinary object contained within time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Yet recognition occurs in the experience of a person who appears to live through temporal succession.
blocks.directed: Yet recognition occurs in the experience of a person who appears to live through temporal succession.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: One moment the person fails to recognise their true nature.
blocks.directed: One moment the person fails to recognise their true nature.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Another moment recognition occurs.
blocks.directed: Another moment recognition occurs.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: How can something timeless be recognised at a particular time?
blocks.directed: How can something timeless be recognised at a particular time?

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Because the temporal occurrence of recognition is not identical with the temporal production of the reality recognised.
blocks.directed: Because the temporal occurrence of recognition is not identical with the temporal production of the reality recognised.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: This distinction is fundamental.
blocks.directed: This distinction is fundamental.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Suppose you fail to recognise someone you know.
blocks.directed: Suppose you fail to recognise someone you know.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: You see them across the street.
blocks.directed: You see them across the street.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: You stare.
blocks.directed: You stare.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: You wonder who they are.
blocks.directed: You wonder who they are.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Suddenly:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Suddenly:

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: “Oh! It's my old friend!”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Oh! It's my old friend!”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The recognition occurs at a particular time.
blocks.directed: The recognition occurs at a particular time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But your friend did not begin existing at the moment you recognised them.
blocks.directed: But your friend did not begin existing at the moment you recognised them.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The event of recognition is temporally located.
blocks.directed: The event of recognition is temporally located.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The recognised identity is not produced by that event.
blocks.directed: The recognised identity is not produced by that event.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: This is an analogy, not a complete account of liberation.
blocks.directed: This is an analogy, not a complete account of liberation.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But it helps clarify the logic.
blocks.directed: But it helps clarify the logic.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The ultimate Self does not begin existing when the practitioner recognises it.
blocks.directed: The ultimate Self does not begin existing when the practitioner recognises it.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The recognition occurs within a particular experiential condition.
blocks.directed: The recognition occurs within a particular experiential condition.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Its object-or more accurately, the reality disclosed by the recognition-is not manufactured at that moment.
blocks.directed: Its object-or more accurately, the reality disclosed by the recognition-is not manufactured at that moment.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Akālakalita
blocks.directed: [slowly] Akālakalita

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Break the compound.
blocks.directed: Break the compound.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: a- - negation.
blocks.directed: a- - negation.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: kāla - time.
blocks.directed: kāla - time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: kalita - reckoned, measured, constructed, determined; related to √kal, to count or calculate.
blocks.directed: kalita - reckoned, measured, constructed, determined; related to √kal, to count or calculate.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: akālakalita - not determined by time.
blocks.directed: akālakalita - not determined by time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The locative akālakalitatve means “in the condition of not being temporally determined.”
blocks.directed: The locative akālakalitatve means “in the condition of not being temporally determined.”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: api introduces the concession: even though.
blocks.directed: api introduces the concession: even though.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Then:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Then:

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: parakalanāpekṣayā
blocks.directed: [slowly] parakalanāpekṣayā

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: para-kalanā-apekṣayā.
blocks.directed: [slowly] para-kalanā-apekṣayā.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: “With reference to another reckoning.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “With reference to another reckoning.”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: apekṣā means reference to, dependence on, or consideration of something.
blocks.directed: apekṣā means reference to, dependence on, or consideration of something.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: This is an instrumental singular.
blocks.directed: This is an instrumental singular.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The point is that temporal language is being used relative to a particular perspective.
blocks.directed: The point is that temporal language is being used relative to a particular perspective.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: From the level of ordinary activity, recognition may be described as occurring instantly.
blocks.directed: From the level of ordinary activity, recognition may be described as occurring instantly.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: From the standpoint of supreme consciousness, that reality is not divided into before and after.
blocks.directed: From the standpoint of supreme consciousness, that reality is not divided into before and after.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Unmeṣa - उन्मेष
blocks.directed: [slowly] Unmeṣa - उन्मेष

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: An opening.
blocks.directed: An opening.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: A blossoming.
blocks.directed: A blossoming.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The opening of an eye.
blocks.directed: The opening of an eye.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: A sudden emergence.
blocks.directed: A sudden emergence.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Related to ud- + √miṣ, to open the eyes, in the relevant verbal family.
blocks.directed: Related to ud- + √miṣ, to open the eyes, in the relevant verbal family.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: You remember the opening verse of the Spandakārikā:
blocks.directed: [short pause] You remember the opening verse of the Spandakārikā:

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: यस्योन्मेषनिमेषाभ्यां
blocks.directed: [slowly] यस्योन्मेषनिमेषाभ्यां

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyām.
blocks.directed: [slowly] yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyām.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: “By whose opening and closing…”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “By whose opening and closing…”

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The oscillation between unmeṣa and nimeṣa is used to describe the emergence and dissolution of manifestation.
blocks.directed: The oscillation between unmeṣa and nimeṣa is used to describe the emergence and dissolution of manifestation.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But the supreme consciousness is not simply another event inside that oscillation.
blocks.directed: But the supreme consciousness is not simply another event inside that oscillation.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: It is the ground through which emergence and withdrawal become possible.
blocks.directed: It is the ground through which emergence and withdrawal become possible.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: So a moment of recognition can be called unmeṣa.
blocks.directed: So a moment of recognition can be called unmeṣa.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: An opening.
blocks.directed: An opening.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: A flash.
blocks.directed: A flash.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Not because the infinite has travelled through time.
blocks.directed: Not because the infinite has travelled through time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But because the limited subject's apprehension has opened into what was already fundamental.
blocks.directed: But because the limited subject's apprehension has opened into what was already fundamental.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: The difference between metaphysical timelessness and distorted time perception
blocks.directed: The difference between metaphysical timelessness and distorted time perception

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: This is worth stressing.
blocks.directed: This is worth stressing.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: A profound meditative experience can involve an altered sense of time.
blocks.directed: A profound meditative experience can involve an altered sense of time.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: An hour may seem short.
blocks.directed: An hour may seem short.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: A moment may seem extraordinarily expansive.
blocks.directed: A moment may seem extraordinarily expansive.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: But those phenomenological changes are not by themselves proof of a timeless metaphysical absolute.
blocks.directed: But those phenomenological changes are not by themselves proof of a timeless metaphysical absolute.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Abhinavagupta's argument is philosophical.
blocks.directed: Abhinavagupta's argument is philosophical.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Consciousness, conceived as the ultimate condition of temporal manifestation, is not itself treated as merely one more temporally delimited object.
blocks.directed: Consciousness, conceived as the ultimate condition of temporal manifestation, is not itself treated as merely one more temporally delimited object.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Experiences of altered time may be interesting.
blocks.directed: Experiences of altered time may be interesting.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: They do not automatically establish that metaphysical claim.
blocks.directed: They do not automatically establish that metaphysical claim.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: Now he turns to smaraṇa, remembering.
blocks.directed: Now he turns to smaraṇa, remembering.

blocks.section: X. Muhūrta: How Long Does Recognition Take If Consciousness
blocks.text: And the next section of the commentary becomes an extraordinarily sophisticated investigation of memory, identity, and the relation between the past and present.
blocks.directed: And the next section of the commentary becomes an extraordinarily sophisticated investigation of memory, identity, and the relation between the past and present.

blocks.directed: [slowly] यः स्मरत्यनुसंधत्ते

blocks.directed: [short pause] “The one who remembers, who connects or integrates.”

blocks.section: XI. The Cosmic Magnet: How Memory Reassembles the Entire Uni
blocks.text: The two verbs are worth distinguishing.

blocks.section: XI. The Cosmic Magnet: How Memory Reassembles the Entire Uni
blocks.text: The second verb is especially important.
blocks.directed: The second verb is especially important.

blocks.section: XI. The Cosmic Magnet: How Memory Reassembles the Entire Uni
blocks.text: This is not just retrieval of a memory-image.
blocks.directed: This is not just retrieval of a memory-image.

blocks.section: XI. The Cosmic Magnet: How Memory Reassembles the Entire Uni

blocks.directed: [short pause] My translation:

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: “Even one who has not seen the maṇḍala, whoever truly knows in this manner, becomes a possessor of accomplishment forever. He is a yogin, and he is initiated.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Even one who has not seen the maṇḍala, whoever truly knows in this manner, becomes a possessor of accomplishment forever. He is a yogin, and he is initiated.”

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: This is the next great turn.
blocks.directed: This is the next great turn.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: Because the text has just spent considerable energy explaining the importance of the guru, transmission, mantric understanding, and ritual disciplines.
blocks.directed: Because the text has just spent considerable energy explaining the importance of the guru, transmission, mantric understanding, and ritual disciplines.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: Now it declares that someone who has not even seen the ritual maṇḍala may nevertheless be an accomplished yogin and an initiate through true knowledge.
blocks.directed: Now it declares that someone who has not even seen the ritual maṇḍala may nevertheless be an accomplished yogin and an initiate through true knowledge.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: The man who hasn't attended the ceremony may nevertheless possess its ultimate result.
blocks.directed: The man who hasn't attended the ceremony may nevertheless possess its ultimate result.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: And that is exactly the paradox Part XXXI must investigate.
blocks.directed: And that is exactly the paradox Part Thirty-One must investigate.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: A textual warning about the numbering
blocks.directed: A textual warning about the numbering

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: The 1918 KSTS presentation numbers this section as verse 18, and GRETIL's commented text agrees in placing adṛṣṭamaṇḍala at the next transition.
blocks.directed: The 1918 KSTS presentation numbers this section as verse 18, and GRETIL's commented text agrees in placing adṛṣṭamaṇḍala at the next transition.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: However, the independently transmitted Parātriṃśikā edited in Marino Faliero's transcription counts the corresponding material differently: it contains an additional line concerning the power of entering the mantra and numbers adṛṣṭamaṇḍala as verse 19.
blocks.directed: However, the independently transmitted Parātriṃśikā edited in Marino Faliero's transcription counts the corresponding material differently: it contains an additional line concerning the power of entering the mantra and numbers adṛṣṭamaṇḍala as verse 19.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: That difference must not be concealed. It reflects a difference in how the root text is transmitted and segmented, not a licence to invent or omit words. ; ; ]
blocks.directed: That difference must not be concealed. It reflects a difference in how the root text is transmitted and segmented, not a licence to invent or omit words. ; ; ]

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: Part XXXI should therefore begin from KSTS verse 18, adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'py evam, explicitly preserving the independent verse-numbering difference.
blocks.directed: Part Thirty-One should therefore begin from KSTS verse 18, adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'py evam, explicitly preserving the independent verse-numbering difference.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: And we stop here.
blocks.directed: And we stop here.

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: Because Abhinavagupta has just raised the next and perhaps most dangerous question in the whole text:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Because Abhinavagupta has just raised the next and perhaps most dangerous question in the whole text:

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: If real initiation is recognition, can someone be truly initiated without performing the prescribed initiation?
blocks.directed: If real initiation is recognition, can someone be truly initiated without performing the prescribed initiation?

blocks.section: XXI. The Next Authentic Transition: The Man Who Has Never Se
blocks.text: And if so, what happens to ritual authority?
blocks.directed: And if so, what happens to ritual authority?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the Fuck Is Teaching Whom?
blocks.directed: [long pause] Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the Fuck Is Teaching Whom?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Let's return to the beginning.
blocks.directed: Let's return to the beginning.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: We started with a guru whose satisfaction apparently determines whether a disciple can receive the supreme mantra.
blocks.directed: We started with a guru whose satisfaction apparently determines whether a disciple can receive the supreme mantra.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The mantra must be transmitted correctly.
blocks.directed: The mantra must be transmitted correctly.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The tradition places restrictions on recording it.
blocks.directed: The tradition places restrictions on recording it.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The teacher must possess the relevant understanding.
blocks.directed: The teacher must possess the relevant understanding.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student must be prepared.
blocks.directed: The student must be prepared.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: A particular ritual order has to be respected.
blocks.directed: A particular ritual order has to be respected.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And yet, at the very heart of this theological structure, Abhinavagupta declares that liberation is nothing other than identity with Bhairava.
blocks.directed: And yet, at the very heart of this theological structure, Abhinavagupta declares that liberation is nothing other than identity with Bhairava.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: How can both be true?
blocks.directed: How can both be true?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Because there are two distinct questions.
blocks.directed: Because there are two distinct questions.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: What is the ultimate nature of liberation?
blocks.directed: What is the ultimate nature of liberation?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And:

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: How does a limited subject come to recognise that nature?
blocks.directed: How does a limited subject come to recognise that nature?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The first concerns identity with universal consciousness.
blocks.directed: The first concerns identity with universal consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The second concerns the differentiated process through which recognition may occur.
blocks.directed: The second concerns the differentiated process through which recognition may occur.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The guru is not a second ultimate reality standing outside Śiva.
blocks.directed: The guru is not a second ultimate reality standing outside Śiva.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student is not an independently existing substance that Śiva must somehow transform into itself.
blocks.directed: The student is not an independently existing substance that Śiva must somehow transform into itself.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The mantra is not a foreign power travelling from one isolated being to another.
blocks.directed: The mantra is not a foreign power travelling from one isolated being to another.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The entire situation takes place within the manifestation of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The entire situation takes place within the manifestation of consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The teacher speaks.
blocks.directed: The teacher speaks.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student hears.
blocks.directed: The student hears.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The meaning becomes intelligible.
blocks.directed: The meaning becomes intelligible.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Recognition may arise.
blocks.directed: Recognition may arise.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And the supposed distance between the two beings is understood through the deeper unity of their conscious ground.
blocks.directed: And the supposed distance between the two beings is understood through the deeper unity of their conscious ground.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But the differentiated situation remains meaningful.
blocks.directed: But the differentiated situation remains meaningful.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The teacher's words can be helpful.
blocks.directed: The teacher's words can be helpful.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: A student's understanding can be incomplete.
blocks.directed: A student's understanding can be incomplete.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The tradition's procedures can serve particular purposes.
blocks.directed: The tradition's procedures can serve particular purposes.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The fact that the whole process ultimately belongs to Śiva does not imply that its individual components are meaningless.
blocks.directed: The fact that the whole process ultimately belongs to Śiva does not imply that its individual components are meaningless.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Nonduality is not the abolition of differentiated reality. It is the recognition of its ultimate ground.
blocks.directed: Nonduality is not the abolition of differentiated reality. It is the recognition of its ultimate ground.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And this explains why Abhinavagupta devotes so much effort to language.
blocks.directed: And this explains why Abhinavagupta devotes so much effort to language.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: An utterance arises.
blocks.directed: An utterance arises.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: It is made of particular sounds.
blocks.directed: It is made of particular sounds.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Those sounds are governed by phonological rules.
blocks.directed: Those sounds are governed by phonological rules.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The words participate in semantic structures.
blocks.directed: The words participate in semantic structures.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The sentence becomes intelligible.
blocks.directed: The sentence becomes intelligible.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Understanding occurs.
blocks.directed: Understanding occurs.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But the possibility of understanding is not itself merely another sound in the sentence.
blocks.directed: But the possibility of understanding is not itself merely another sound in the sentence.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The ground of intelligibility is more fundamental than any particular expression.
blocks.directed: The ground of intelligibility is more fundamental than any particular expression.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Similarly, a teacher can communicate the doctrine of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Similarly, a teacher can communicate the doctrine of consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But the consciousness through which the student understands the teaching is not manufactured by the teacher's utterance.
blocks.directed: But the consciousness through which the student understands the teaching is not manufactured by the teacher's utterance.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: It was already present as the condition of hearing anything at all.
blocks.directed: It was already present as the condition of hearing anything at all.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: That is the extraordinary insight toward which the passage moves.
blocks.directed: That is the extraordinary insight toward which the passage moves.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The guru does not install consciousness.
blocks.directed: The guru does not install consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The mantra does not import consciousness.
blocks.directed: The mantra does not import consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The ritual does not create consciousness.
blocks.directed: The ritual does not create consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The teaching makes possible the recognition of what was never absent.
blocks.directed: The teaching makes possible the recognition of what was never absent.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And that is why the next verse is explosive.
blocks.directed: And that is why the next verse is explosive.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student who has never seen the maṇḍala may nevertheless be initiated.
blocks.directed: The student who has never seen the maṇḍala may nevertheless be initiated.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Not because rites are automatically worthless.
blocks.directed: Not because rites are automatically worthless.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But because the supreme purpose of initiation is not finally exhausted by the external rite.
blocks.directed: But because the supreme purpose of initiation is not finally exhausted by the external rite.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The question becomes whether the inner transformation has occurred.
blocks.directed: The question becomes whether the inner transformation has occurred.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The ritual points toward that transformation.
blocks.directed: The ritual points toward that transformation.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The guru teaches that transformation.
blocks.directed: The guru teaches that transformation.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The mantra expresses that transformation.
blocks.directed: The mantra expresses that transformation.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But the reality disclosed is not an object belonging to the guru, the ritual, or the manuscript.
blocks.directed: But the reality disclosed is not an object belonging to the guru, the ritual, or the manuscript.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: It is the very nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: It is the very nature of consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The teacher looks at the student.
blocks.directed: The teacher looks at the student.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student looks at the teacher.
blocks.directed: The student looks at the teacher.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Both are manifestations of the same supreme subject.
blocks.directed: Both are manifestations of the same supreme subject.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: And somewhere in eleventh-century Kashmir, Abhinavagupta is probably laughing at the fact that the entire universe has organised an elaborate ceremony so that consciousness can remind itself that it is consciousness.
blocks.directed: And somewhere in eleventh-century Kashmir, Abhinavagupta is probably laughing at the fact that the entire universe has organised an elaborate ceremony so that consciousness can remind itself that it is consciousness.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The alphabet has completed its lesson.
blocks.directed: The alphabet has completed its lesson.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The guru has finished speaking.
blocks.directed: The guru has finished speaking.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: The student has heard the words.
blocks.directed: The student has heard the words.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: But the real question is no longer what the teacher said.
blocks.directed: But the real question is no longer what the teacher said.

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: It is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] It is:

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: Who, precisely, was present to hear it?
blocks.directed: Who, precisely, was present to hear it?

blocks.section: Closing: The Guru Is Śiva. The Student Is Śiva. So Who the F
blocks.text: End of Part XXX - the commentary through the conclusion of the explanation of verses 10-17, ending at the introduction of the verse beginning adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'py evam.
blocks.directed: End of Part Thirty - the commentary through the conclusion of the explanation of verses 10-17, ending at the introduction of the verse beginning adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'py evam.
